text:
oncall-bot: URGENT: SRE Alert — severity=P2 | region=us-east-1 | reason=GPU pool saturated, queue growth > 2k reqs, autoscale failed to provision 3rd batch (error: quota_exceeded). Paging on-call. https://internal.ops/alerts/1792501123 :rotating_light:

alex: paging — I'm on it, grabbing logs and current ASG state. seeing sustained GPU util 98% on east1-gpu-pool-01..04. queue length 2.1k and climbing.

mira: oncall here. tagging @jordan for routing rules (cross-region spillover). Is east-west routing enabled for east1?

jordan: yes it is. Routing policy: prefer local, spillover to us-west-2 after 75% queue latency threshold. Looks like the routing decision loop is delayed — I see failed attempts to register new west nodes: "connection timeout to control-plane".

emily: customer-impact tracker: several high-volume tenants reporting 503s, increased latency. Top affected: search-api-prod, chat-async-batch. Notifying CS.

alex: grabbing autoscaler logs. Found repeated errors: 
```
2026-03-14T09:34:01Z autoscaler: request_scale(count=3) -> failed (quota_exceeded)
2026-03-14T09:34:04Z autoscaler: retrying -> failed (rate_limited)
2026-03-14T09:34:09Z autoscaler: fallback -> unable_to_provision
```

patrick: Ops quota was recently lowered in us-east-1 for burst buffer — I'm checking infra tickets. If quota_exceeded then autoscaler won't spawn new GPU nodes.

mira: can we trigger manual spillover to us-west-2 while infra works quotas? Need a quick mitigation to reduce queue.

jordan: I can flip a temporary policy to force-route 30% of traffic to us-west-2 for specific prefixes (search/chat) — but note some models pinned to east1 with local KV cache; cross-region will incur cold KV misses. Expect degraded throughput initially. Confirm?

emily: confirm. We should notify customers about degraded but available service vs complete outage. Prepare status message: "High latency and intermittent 503 in US-EAST for inference; we are rerouting traffic to alternative region and working on scaling."

alex: manual mitigation steps I'm doing now: 1) disable local-only routing for model group alpha-llama-13b, 2) create temporary route policy force-route:us-west-2 for /v1/generate with weight=0.3, 3) throttle lower-priority background jobs. Executing 1/3 now.

oncall-bot: ACTION: Incident assigned to mira, severity=P2, runbook=https://internal.runbooks/gpu-saturation

mira: Route change applied (policy id r-179250). Monitoring queue impact. Also triggered throttle on batch-ingest:priority=low.

alex: queue dropped from 2.1k -> 900 within 90s after route flip. latency for forced requests to west jumped ~400ms initially, then stabilized to +120ms.

emily: status update for customers drafted. Will publish in 5 min.

jordan: while routing change helped, control-plane still returning intermittent timeouts when registering west workers. There are 5/12 register errors showing TLS handshake timeout. Sharing logs: 
```
ERROR control-plane: tls handshake timeout from us-west-2-agent-12 -> 300s
```

patrick: I have infra on call opening a ticket with cloud provider for quota bump and TLS handshake investigation. ETA 30-45m.

sre-lead: decision point — do we continue forced spillover or revert and accept higher latency? Also need to coordinate handoff at +30m.

mira: keep forced spillover for now. Also enabling conservative admission control on east1 to keep latencies for highest-priority tenants: set token bucket for search-api-prod to limit 80 QPS.

alex: applied admission control: search-api-prod = 80 QPS, chat-async-batch = 50 QPS. Should reduce tail latencies.

emily: published status: "Experiencing GPU saturation in us-east-1 causing increased latency and 503s. We are routing a portion of traffic to us-west-2 and throttling non-critical workloads. Engineers are working on autoscaling & infra quota issues. ETA 45m." Posted to status.redwood.com and notified enterprise contacts. :loudspeaker:

mira: @eng-platform, can you confirm model pin overrides for any enterprise customers — we don't want to silently route to west if they opted in to east-only?

eng-platform: checking customer model pin table — found 3 enterprise tenants pinned to east1 for compliance. Reached out to their account owners; created temporary exception list so we don't route them. Force-route applied to all others.

jordan: TL;DR mitigations: forced partial spillover -> queue reduced; admission control -> lower tail latency for top tenants; manual throttles on background jobs -> freed capacity; infra ticket open for quota & TLS. Next: monitor and plan canary rollback once quota restored.

oncall-bot: NOTE: new alert — replication lag for KV cache in us-west-2 increased to 12s due to cold starts. Potential model perf regressions.

alex: we're seeing some model error rate uptick (sanity checks failing on generation length). Rolling back forced spillover for small % to allow cache warmup then increasing weight gradually.

emily: updated status to customers: "We are seeing degraded model outputs for some requests routed to the fallback region while caches warm. We are monitoring and adjusting traffic to balance latency vs quality."

patrick: cloud provider acknowledged quota request, preliminary approval for +4 gpus in 22m, full ticket in progress. TLS handshake errors still under investigation.

mira: handoff plan: I'm staying for 30m, then handing to alex for follow-up until quota resolved. @sre-lead will take incident lead after that. Documenting action items in the runbook.

sre-lead: received handoff. Next steps: validate provider quota uplift, confirm TLS handshake root cause, coordinate a controlled autoscaler re-enable (dry run), and prepare postmortem with customer impact table.

jordan: adding note — we need a new control-plane circuit breaker so routing changes don't stall when control-plane has transient timeouts. Filing eng-ticket now.

emily: CS has notified 4 enterprise customers and escalated one who runs compliance workload. They accepted the temporary exception.

alex: final note before handoff: overall mitigation reduced queue by ~70% and restored service for most tenants. Residual impacts: 1) some requests in west had higher latency and occasional quality regressions, 2) three enterprise tenants still served from east and saw partial throttling.

oncall-bot: INCIDENT: severity downgraded to P3 at 1792501900 - autoscaling partial recovery in progress.

mira: handing off now to alex, will stay reachable if needed.

alex: acknowledged handoff. continuing monitoring; will follow up with post-incident timeline and impact summary once quotas confirmed.

emily: publishing final interim customer note: "Stability improving; we will provide another update within 1 hour or when autoscaling fully recovers."

sre-lead: logging timeline + immediate actions to the incident channel and will schedule postmortem for tomorrow. Closing live page but keeping on-call rotation for follow-up. :white_check_mark:
